subject.title: Feature: Distinguish webchat client types (Mac app vs browser)

question: Should agent-visible WebChat client type be exposed as gateway-attested connect metadata, as an explicitly untrusted client hint, or not exposed to agents yet?
rationale: Agents may use this metadata for native-only behavior, deep links, diagnostics, or capability decisions, so automation should not choose the trust semantics or carrier shape without maintainer security/product intent.

options.title: Gateway-attested metadata
options.body: Propagate validated connect.client identity into a narrow runtime metadata field and document what agents may trust.

options.title: Untrusted diagnostic hint
options.body: Expose a clearly labeled untrusted client hint for debugging only and forbid capability or permission decisions from using it.

options.title: Keep runtime exposure closed
options.body: Limit client identity to Gateway diagnostics until a stronger client-attestation design is approved.

recommendation.title: Gateway-attested metadata
recommendation.body: Propagate validated connect.client identity into a narrow runtime metadata field and document what agents may trust.

likelyOwner.reason: The relevant decision sits at the Gateway protocol/client metadata boundary where prior gateway-client extraction work is concentrated.
